Attach the following policy, replacing the example values with your own AWS Region, account ID, and AWS KMS key ID to allow Amazon Bedrock to encrypt the session context.\\n\\n#### Using JSON\\n\\n#### Using\\n\\n```\\n{\\n \\\"Version\\\":\\\"2012-10-17\\\",\\n \\\"Statement\\\": [\\n {\\n \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Allow\\\",\\n \\\"Principal\\\": {\\n \\\"Service\\\": \\\"bedrock.amazonaws.com\\\"\\n },\\n \\\"Action\\\": [\\n \\\"kms:GenerateDataKey\\\",\\n \\\"kms:Decrypt\\\"\\n ],\\n \\\"Resource\\\": \\\"[redacted ARN]\\\"\\n }\\n ]\\n}\\n\\n```\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/encryption-kb.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Build a self-service student assistant with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases\",\"context\":\"### Prerequisites\\n\\nBefore you begin, make sure that you have the following:\\n\\n- An AWS account with access to [Amazon Bedrock](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/).\\n\\n- An S3 bucket to store your source documents.\\n\\n- AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to [create a knowledge base](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/knowledge-base-prereq-permissions-general.html) and read from your [S3 bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security_iam_service-with-iam.html).\\n\\n **Note:** If you create the knowledge base through the AWS Management Console, then Amazon Bedrock can create a service role with the required permissions.\\n\\n- Access to a foundation model to use for answers and an embeddings model to use for vectors.\\n\\n **Note:** In most AWS Regions, [model access is activated by default](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-access.html). Amazon Bedrock keeps your information confidential, and doesn't share the information with model providers or use the information to improve models. Model containers undergo vulnerability scanning. Additionally, Amazon Bedrock Serverless and Amazon Bedrock Marketplace both force network isolation to prevent unauthorized egress of customer data from model containers.\\n\\nTo safely build generative AI applications at scale, [Amazon Bedrock Guardrails](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/guardrails/) uses content filtering, Personally Identifiable Information (PII) redaction, and enhanced safety and privacy measures. You can customize policies to meet specific needs and responsible AI standards. These policies can include the following actions:\\n\\n- Block unwanted topics\\n\\n- Filter specific content and words\\n\\n- Remove PII\\n\\n- Conduct contextual grounding checks\\n\\n- Identify AI hallucinations\\n\\nAWS facilitates robust security and compliance in its AI services through built-in safeguards in Amazon Bedrock and SageMaker AI. These safeguards include the following:\\n\\n- Encryption to protect data, both at rest and in transit\\n\\n- [Access management through IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/introduction.html)\\n\\n- Network security with Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) and [AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/usingVPC.html)\\n\\n- Security groups and network access control lists (network ACLs) to restrict access\\n\\n- CloudWatch and CloudTrail to monitor [Amazon Bedrock performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/monitoring.html#br-cloudwatch-metrics) and [Amazon Bedrock API calls](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/logging-using-cloudtrail.html).\\n\\nConclusion\\n----------\\n\\nThis article demonstrates how to restrict DeepSeek models to follow best practices for the security of your data across your organization.\\n\\nTo get the most out of your AWS environment, contact AWS Cloud Support Engineers and Technical Account Managers (TAMs). They can help you with general guidance, best practices, troubleshooting, and operational support on AWS. To learn more about our plans and offerings, see\u00a0[AWS Support](https://aws.amazon.com/premiumsupport/tam-engagement/). To learn more about the suggested solution, contact your TAM or AWS account team.\\n\\n------------------------------------\\n# About the author\\n\\n![Enter image description here](/media/postImages/original/IMfbAMmN8\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/articles/AROjoxvT7dR-aPBCuLBpVclg/implementing-deepseek-ai-model-restrictions-across-your-aws-organization\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search docs for Bedrock knowledge base encryption check"}
